ctx.x: Hal McIntyre. I did a couple of things for him, not many. He was playing upstate New York in a fabulous nightclub, if I remember correctly. And, you know, he played good sax, he did -- brilliant tone and whatnot. But he wanted -- he didn't want the wild stuff, if I remember correctly. He wanted something, because of the type of exclusive engagements that he played, he wanted something that was not too far out, but yet it had a beat -- I remember him from this, you know. So I made a couple of things for him.

You know, in New York there were quite a few guys during that era, like there was a great arranger named Fred Norman. He was in Claude Hopkins' band, and he was a trombonist and he wrote real good, you know, and -- oh, a guy named Andy Gibson. He was with Charlie Barnett. We were in there together. Now he wrote a lot of things. And -- I'm mentioning these things to say that in those days they had a lot of free lance arrangers, you know, and we used to -- in that thing when I say we, because I was scuffling at…
